message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta.**  
Atlanta’s noise‑related issues are handled through the city’s **Code Enforcement** and **Police Department** offices. Below is a quick guide on how to report a noise problem, what the city’s noise ordinance covers, and the main contact points.

---

## 1. Where to File a Noise Complaint

| Channel | How to Use | Contact Info |
|---------|------------|--------------|
| **Online Form** | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official “Noise Complaint” page and fill out the form. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311/noise-complaint> |
| **Phone (311)** | Call 311 (or 404‑656‑3111) from within Atlanta. The dispatcher will route your call to the appropriate department. | 404‑656‑3111 |
| **Email** | Send a brief description of the issue to 311@atlantaga.gov. | 311@atlantaga.gov |
| **In‑person** | Go to City Hall (1400 Peachtree Street NW, Atlanta, GA 30303) during business hours. Ask for the Code Enforcement or Police Department. | 404‑656‑3111 (for directions) |
| **911** | If the noise is part of an emergency (e.g., a fire, active shooter, or other immediate danger), call 911. | 911 |

> **Tip:** For repeated or ongoing noise problems, it’s often helpful to keep a log (date, time, description, location, and any witnesses). This information can speed up the investigation.

---

## 2. Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 2)

- **Allowed Noise Levels** – The ordinance sets maximum decibel limits for residential and commercial zones, varying by time of day (e.g., stricter limits after 10 p.m.).
- **Prohibited Activities** – Includes loud music, amplified sound equipment, and operating machinery that exceeds the permitted decibel levels.
- **Enforcement** – Violations can result in citations, fines, or, in severe cases, civil or criminal penalties.
- **Public Nuisance** – Persistent noise that interferes with the normal enjoyment of property can be treated as a public nuisance.

> **Link to the full ordinance:** <https://www.atlantaga.gov/DocumentCenter/View/12345/Noise-Ordinance>

---

## 3. What Happens After You File

1. **Acknowledgment** – You’ll receive a confirmation (email or phone) with a case number.
2. **Investigation** – A city officer will visit the site, measure noise levels, and interview witnesses if needed.
3. **Resolution** – Depending on the findings, the officer may issue a warning, citation, or direct the offending party to take corrective action.
4. **Follow‑up** – If the problem persists, you can request a follow‑up inspection or escalation to the City Attorney’s Office.

---

## 4. Quick Checklist Before Filing

- **Identify the source** (e.g., neighbor’s party, construction site, loud music).
- **Record the time and duration** of the disturbance.
- **Take photos or audio recordings** (if safe and legal to do so).
- **Note any witnesses** who can corroborate your claim.
- **Check the zoning** of the property (residential vs. commercial) to understand the applicable noise limits.

---

## 5. Additional Resources

- **Atlanta Police Department – Noise Complaints**: <https://www.atlantapd.org/noise-complaints>
- **City of Atlanta 311 Portal**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311>
- **Atlanta Code Enforcement**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/code-enforcement>
- **City Attorney’s Office (Public Nuisance)**: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/city-attorney>

---

### Bottom Line

Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 system, the online form, or contact the Police/Code Enforcement directly. The city has clear procedures and an ordinance in place to protect residents from excessive noise. If you’re dealing with a persistent issue, keep detailed records and follow up with the city’s enforcement team.
